blocks.source: Vol IV, Safety Enforcement, § Historical Perspective and Further Reading
blocks.md: The safety certificates developed in this chapter trace their intellectual lineage to classical questions about boundary invariance that predate digital computing. In 1892, Aleksandr Lyapunov demonstrated that one can prove the asymptotic stability of a dynamical system by constructing a scalar, energy-like function, bypassing the intractable problem of solving nonlinear differential equations directly.

questions.q: The section **Historical Perspective and Further Reading** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Available deceleration is net of gravity and bias in the worst direction, and integrator unwinding and saturation spend it before the stop begins.

Speed and separation monitoring keeps a protective separation distance (the person's travel, the robot's reaction and stopping travel, intrusion distance, and position uncertainties) between a moving arm and a person as a certified function.
When contact is the task the kinetic barrier admits only zero speed, so an energy-tank passivity barrier and a separately qualified force channel replace clearance as the margin.

A control barrier function makes its safe set forward invariant only if every admitted input keeps hdot >= -alpha(h), and a barrier on raw distance has relative degree two in torque, so the barrier must carry the cost to stop.
